{{Short description|Property in algebraic topology}}
In [[mathematics]], in the area of [[algebraic topology]], the '''homotopy extension property''' indicates which [[homotopy|homotopies]] defined on a [[subspace topology|subspace]] can be extended to a homotopy defined on a larger space.  The homotopy extension property of [[cofibration]]s is [[Eckmann–Hilton duality|dual to]] the [[homotopy lifting property]] that is used to define [[fibration]]s.

==Definition==
Let <math>X\,\!</math> be a [[topological space]], and let <math>A \subset X</math>. We say that the pair <math>(X,A)\,\!</math> has the '''homotopy extension property''' if, given a homotopy <math>f_\bullet\colon A \rightarrow Y^I</math> and a map <math>\tilde{f}_0\colon X \rightarrow Y</math> such that <math display="block">\tilde{f}_0\circ \iota = \left.\tilde{f}_0\right|_A = f_0 = \pi_0 \circ f_\bullet,</math> then there exists an ''extension'' of <math>f_\bullet</math> to a homotopy <math>\tilde{f}_\bullet\colon X \rightarrow Y^I</math> such that <math>\tilde{f}_\bullet\circ \iota = \left.\tilde{f}_\bullet\right|_A = f_\bullet</math>.<ref>A. Dold, ''Lectures on Algebraic Topology'', pp. 84, Springer {{ISBN|3-540-58660-1}}</ref>

That is, the pair <math>(X,A)\,\!</math> has the homotopy extension property if any map <math>G\colon ((X\times \{0\}) \cup (A\times I)) \rightarrow Y</math> can be extended to a map <math>G'\colon X\times I \rightarrow Y</math> (i.e. <math>G\,\!</math> and <math>G'\,\!</math> agree on their common domain).

If the pair has this property only for a certain [[codomain]] <math>Y\,\!</math>, we say that <math>(X,A)\,\!</math> has the homotopy extension property with respect to <math>Y\,\!</math>.

==Visualisation==
The homotopy extension property is depicted in the following diagram

[[File:Homotopy extension property rotated.svg|175px|center]]

If the above diagram (without the dashed map) commutes (this is equivalent to the conditions above), then pair (X,A) has the homotopy extension property if there exists a map <math>\tilde{f}_\bullet</math> which makes the diagram commute. By [[currying]], note that homotopies expressed as maps <math>\tilde{f}_\bullet \colon X \to Y^I</math> are in [[Natural transformation#Tensor-hom adjunction| natural bijection]] with expressions as maps <math> \tilde{f}_\bullet \colon X\times I \to Y </math>.

Note that this diagram is dual to (opposite to) that of the [[homotopy lifting property]]; this duality is loosely referred to as [[Eckmann–Hilton duality]].

==Examples==
* Any CW pair <math>(X,A)\,\!</math> (that is, <math>X\,\!</math> is a [[cell complex]] and <math>A\,\!</math> is a subcomplex of <math>X\,\!</math>) has the homotopy extension property.<ref>{{cite book | first = Allen | last = Hatcher | authorlink = Allen Hatcher | year = 2002 | title = Algebraic Topology | publisher  = Cambridge University Press | isbn = 0-521-79540-0 | page=15 | url = https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATpage.html}} Proposition 0.16</ref>

==Properties==
* A pair <math>(X,A)\,\!</math> has the homotopy extension property if and only if <math>(X\times \{0\} \cup A\times I)</math> is a [[Deformation retract|retract]] of <math>X\times I.</math><ref>{{cite book | first = Allen | last = Hatcher | authorlink = Allen Hatcher | year = 2002 | title = Algebraic Topology | publisher  = Cambridge University Press | isbn = 0-521-79540-0 | page=14 | url = https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATpage.html}}</ref>

==Other==
If <math>(X, A)</math> has the homotopy extension property, then the simple inclusion map <math>\iota\colon A \to X</math> is a [[cofibration]].

In fact, if <math>\iota\colon Y \to Z</math> is a [[cofibration]], then <math>\mathbf{\mathit{Y}}</math> is [[homeomorphic]] to its image under <math>\iota</math>. This implies that any cofibration can be treated as an inclusion map, and therefore it can be treated as having the homotopy extension property.
